summary: Hebrew uses one word for the thumb of the hand and the big toe of the foot. The priestly rites name each in turn. Judges uses a single plural to cover both.

senses.definition: The first digit of a hand or foot. The adjoining body-part noun identifies which is meant.

evidence.note: The ordination instructions pair the thumb of the right hand with the big toe of the right foot.
Moses marks both digits on Aaron.
Aaron’s sons receive the same markings.
The blood of the guilt offering is applied to both digits of the person being cleansed.
The priest applies oil over the blood on the hand and foot.
Blood goes on the same two digits in the provision for a poor worshipper.
The oil is applied to the places already marked with blood.
Adoni-bezek’s captors cut off the digits of his hands and feet.
He recalls inflicting the same injury on seventy kings.

note: Kogan, Proto-Semitic Lexicon §6.3.1.2, cites the Ebla spelling ba-ʾà-núm (VE 499) and compares Mehri hābēn and Harsusi ḥābēn ‘thumb’. The Arabic word has final m where Hebrew has n. The Akkadian form denotes a finger more generally. The name Bohan occurs in Joshua’s boundary descriptions.
